You can find a more diplomatic, or politically convenient description for it, but the Modi government’s latest move on the Agniveer scheme, brought in with such aplomb, is a rollback. More so, a poll-eve capitulation. In this week’s , ThePrint Editor-in-Chief Shekhar Gupta examines how between the farm laws and Agnipath, the govt erred in taking its most loyal constituencies for granted: Hindi-heartland farmers & soldiers, and how poor planning and a failure to build public acceptance led to the collapse of both reforms.
